title: Scale Carbon Projects with Reliable MRV
headline: Scale Carbon Projects with Reliable MRV
question: How might we improve measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) and expand small carbon projects through suitable partnerships to build a scalable portfolio of credible emissions reductions and removals?
background: A shipping and logistics group wants to develop carbon projects beyond its existing small initiatives. Its projects are individually too small to scale efficiently, and limited access to underlying land creates additional investment and development challenges.

The objective is to establish reliable project-level MRV, identify suitable projects and partners, and expand through joint operations, joint ventures or dedicated project companies. Relevant startup capabilities include carbon project development, environmental monitoring, geospatial analysis and project documentation.
Nature-based innovation is the main focus. Other non-blue-carbon project types are also welcome; blue carbon is excluded.

significance.label: Limited project expansion
significance.body: Small initiatives lack the scale needed to form a larger, viable portfolio.

significance.label: Higher development costs
significance.body: Separate monitoring and documentation processes increase the cost of developing individual projects.

significance.label: Verification delays
significance.body: Incomplete baseline data, monitoring records and supporting evidence slow assessment and verification.

significance.label: Investment barriers
significance.body: Gaps in land access, project rights and partner expertise slow investment decisions.

efforts.label: Current company approach
efforts.body: The group has developed an internal carbon calculator. It is now seeking additional project-development and MRV capabilities to support expansion.

efforts.label: Available partner capabilities
efforts.body: A nature-based project provider offers individual-tree tracking and a partnership supporting project development and verification documentation. A geospatial assessment provider offers land-boundary validation, supplier-evidence collection and forest-risk analysis. A secure document platform provides controlled access to project records and supporting evidence.

efforts.label: Implementation priorities
efforts.body: Connect project screening, monitoring and evidence preparation within a carbon-specific MRV process. Establish a practical approach to expanding or combining suitable projects, and incorporate independent validation and verification into the project lifecycle.

market.label: Growing verification-services market
market.body: A September 2026 estimate places the global carbon-credit validation, verification and certification services market at US$366.6 million in 2025, rising to US$2.07 billion by 2033, with 24.2% annual growth during 2026–2033. This category covers project assessment and certification services, including activities beyond digital MRV software.

market.label: Project expansion potential in Indonesia
market.body: Indonesia announced a target in October 2026 to rehabilitate 12 million hectares of degraded land. This creates a substantial landscape for project assessment and monitoring. Carbon-project development must establish eligibility for each selected site.

market.label: Regulatory demand for verification
market.body: Indonesia’s Minister of Forestry Regulation No. 6 of 2026 requires validation and verification of forestry carbon units, including checks on baselines, additionality and achieved results. These requirements support demand for reliable project data and verification support.

title: Automate Freight Accounting and Trigger Invoicing from Delivery Evidence
headline: Automate Freight Accounting and Trigger Invoicing from Delivery Evidence
question: How might we automate freight accounting and use accepted proof of delivery to trigger accurate customer invoicing in the ERP?

The objective is to reduce repeated data entry, improve accounting consistency and shorten the handover from completed delivery to customer billing. Once POD is accepted and agreed billing conditions are satisfied, the ERP must issue the corresponding invoice through the defined approval process.

efforts.body: Extend the workflow from supplier-invoice automation and accounts payable to customer invoicing. background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer also operates ready-to-eat, ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook product lines. This project focuses on production efficiency, with the production team selecting the priority process and defining success measures during pilot planning.

The objective is to establish a shared view of production steps, material movements, equipment use and output. This gives the operating team a basis for distinguishing capacity constraints from waiting, downtime and process variation before choosing an improvement.

Relevant startup capabilities include manufacturing execution systems, equipment monitoring, industrial data integration and production analytics. Selection criteria include equipment connectivity, available records and compatibility with the food-production environment.

significance.label: Unclear improvement priorities
significance.body: An incomplete operating baseline directs investment toward activities with limited influence on production performance.

significance.label: Harder production planning
significance.body: Limited visibility of actual output and equipment availability makes realistic production schedules difficult to establish.

significance.label: Unmeasured operating costs
significance.body: Waiting, stoppages and repeated work consume capacity, while incomplete records obscure their full effect.

efforts.label: Available capabilities
efforts.body: A manufacturing digitalisation provider offers production tracking, industrial IoT and internal material-movement automation. An equipment-monitoring platform consolidates machine, sensor and operating data to analyse performance and downtime. The pilot will assess these capabilities against the retailer’s production requirements.

efforts.label: First application
efforts.body: Select one production step and compare recorded input, saleable output, operating time and stoppage reasons with direct observation. Agree who reviews the information and which decisions it supports.

efforts.label: Implementation priorities
efforts.body: Establish asset and process fit, the cost of data capture, integration requirements and a measurable improvement target. Connect monitoring results to a defined process change and evaluate its effect on production performance.

title: Test Flexible Robotics for Repetitive Food Handling
headline: Test Flexible Robotics for Repetitive Food Handling
question: How might we automate a suitable repetitive food-handling task while maintaining product integrity, hygiene and a practical production cycle time?
background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer operates prepared-food lines using ingredients also sold through its retail business. This project focuses on improving production efficiency through a repetitive food-handling task selected with the production team.

The objective is to identify one handling, positioning or assembly task where automation delivers measurable value. A workable solution must accommodate representative variations in food shape, texture, moisture and fragility under realistic conditions.

Relevant partner capabilities include robotic grippers, machine vision, robot integration and food-production engineering. Pilot planning will document task volumes, manual effort, cleaning procedures and acceptable product-damage rates.

significance.label: Poor automation decisions
significance.body: Equipment spending without a task-specific feasibility test leads to limited operating value or substantial redesign.

significance.label: Capacity constraints
significance.body: Repetitive manual bottlenecks limit the output achievable from the wider production process.

significance.label: Inconsistent handling
significance.body: An unsuitable automated approach damages products or adds interruptions, reducing the productivity benefit.

efforts.label: Available research
efforts.body: An adjustable robotic gripper research prototype uses configurable fingers, adjustable stiffness and interchangeable gripping mechanisms for foods with different characteristics. At TRL3, it provides an early proof of concept for integration into a production-cell trial.

efforts.label: First application
efforts.body: Choose one product and one task. Compare grasp reliability, placement accuracy, cycle time, product damage and cleaning effort against the current method using representative samples.

efforts.label: Implementation priorities
efforts.body: Integrate the prototype with a robot and controls, assess food-contact materials, incorporate hygienic design and validate cleaning procedures. A specialist integrator and the company’s quality team must establish a suitable test setup before production use. Qualify additional products and tasks through separate trials before broadening the application.

title: Develop Suitable and Appealing Prepared-Food Packaging
headline: Develop Suitable and Appealing Prepared-Food Packaging
question: How might we improve prepared-food packaging presentation and select alternative materials that fit the product, handling and preparation conditions?
background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer operates ready-to-eat, ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook lines. This project addresses attractive packaging through improvements to materials, format and presentation. The company will define detailed product and packaging requirements during pilot planning.

The objective is to develop a pack that presents the food clearly, suits customer use and performs through the intended storage and distribution conditions. Environmental claims and material-performance claims must be supported by relevant evidence.

Relevant startup capabilities include packaging materials, structural design, printing, sealing and manufacturing services. Select a representative product and document the current pack, filling method and intended preparation conditions before choosing a material.

significance.label: Weak product presentation
significance.body: Unclear packaging information makes purchasing and preparation more difficult for customers.

significance.label: Packaging incompatibility
significance.body: An unsuitable material or seal fails during filling, handling, storage or intended preparation.

significance.label: Poor investment returns
significance.body: Material changes without evidence on cost, machinability and performance increase expense without delivering the intended benefit.

efforts.label: Available material capability
efforts.body: A packaging-material developer produces biodegradable films using agricultural residues and publishes material specifications. These specifications provide the starting point for selecting samples and testing food-contact suitability and performance for the retailer’s products.

efforts.label: Implementation priorities
efforts.body: Establish sample supply, food-contact documentation, barrier properties, sealing compatibility and any heating or freezing requirements. title: Establish and Extend Prepared-Food Shelf Life
headline: Establish and Extend Prepared-Food Shelf Life
question: How might we establish the shelf life of a selected prepared-food product and test changes that extend it while maintaining safety and acceptable quality?
background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer operates ready-to-eat, ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook product lines. This project focuses on longer shelf life, with the company selecting the product, documenting its current shelf life and setting a target during pilot planning.

The objective is to identify the factors limiting a selected product’s usable life and evaluate suitable changes to packaging, processing or storage. Any longer shelf-life claim must be supported by product-specific evidence under the intended distribution and use conditions.

Relevant partner capabilities include food-preservation technology, packaging expertise, microbiological testing and sensory evaluation. Select the approach using the recipe, preparation process, storage temperature and intended customer use.

significance.label: Limited selling flexibility
significance.body: A short selling period restricts distribution and production-planning options.

significance.label: Product-quality deterioration
significance.body: Changes without appropriate testing compromise the qualities customers expect throughout the claimed shelf life.

significance.label: Unsupported commercial decisions

title: Track Fresh Inventory from Purchase to Sale or Loss
headline: Track Fresh Inventory from Purchase to Sale or Loss
question: How might we make fresh and frozen inventory movements, markdowns and losses visible by product and outlet to identify where improvements create value?
background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer sells fresh, frozen and prepared foods through physical and online channels. This project focuses on inventory yield by establishing a clear record of spoilage, markdowns and stock write-offs across a selected part of the business.

The objective is to measure how purchased inventory becomes sales, transfers, markdowns, processing inputs or recorded losses. Use this baseline to quantify the value at stake and select a focused intervention.

Relevant startup capabilities include inventory software, batch and date records, stock-count tools and operational analytics. Pilot planning will document current systems and record availability, then select the product category and outlets for the trial.

significance.label: Hidden loss drivers
significance.body: Unexplained stock adjustments and markdowns obscure where inventory value is being reduced.

significance.label: Harder improvement decisions
significance.body: Incomplete records prevent effective comparison of purchasing, handling, allocation and preservation options.

significance.label: Unreliable financial measurement
significance.body: Treating transfers, processing inputs, physical waste and reduced selling prices as the same event overstates savings and obscures their causes.

efforts.label: Existing operating context
efforts.body: The retailer checks freshness, condition, cleanliness, packaging and dates. Build on these quality controls by mapping how staff record inventory movements and losses.

efforts.label: Available capability
efforts.body: Configurable inventory software tracks purchases, receipts, transfers, sales, counts and adjustments across locations. Configure food-specific batch, date, loss-reason and quantity fields to match the retailer’s workflow.

efforts.label: First application
efforts.body: Track one category through a small group of outlets and reconcile system movements with physical counts. Establish a baseline by quantity and value, then review the largest measured loss reasons. Measure visibility improvements separately from subsequent interventions and count each benefit once across allocation, preservation and product conversion.

title: Preserve Quality for Suitable Fresh-Fruit Products
headline: Preserve Quality for Suitable Fresh-Fruit Products
question: How might we preserve the quality of compatible fresh fruit for longer under the retailer’s actual storage and handling conditions?
background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer handles fresh produce alongside other grocery and prepared-food categories. This project focuses on fresh-fruit preservation, using fruit-specific loss and quality measurements to select a practical intervention.

The objective is to improve saleable quality for a selected fruit at an acceptable additional cost. The trial must reflect the actual maturity, supply route, storage conditions and handling practices involved.

Relevant partner capabilities include edible coatings, post-harvest treatment, application equipment and produce-quality assessment. Establish compatibility for each fruit individually and keep performance claims specific to the tested fruit and conditions.

significance.label: Reduced saleable quality
significance.body: Deterioration leaves fruit in an unacceptable condition before its intended sale.

significance.label: Lower value recovery
significance.body: A short effective selling period creates markdown pressure or unsold stock when demand and timing do not align.

significance.label: Unproductive treatment costs
significance.body: A coating unsuited to the fruit or storage conditions adds handling and material costs without a commercial benefit.

efforts.label: Available research capability
efforts.body: A university plant-derived edible-coating technology regulates gas exchange and provides antibacterial and antifungal protection for compatible fruits, including mangoes, avocados and papayas. The technology is reported at TRL6 with laboratory and field testing. Use fruit-specific trials to establish its performance within the retailer’s supply chain.

efforts.label: First application
efforts.body: Choose a compatible fruit and compare treated and untreated batches with similar maturity and handling. Review quality over time, acceptable selling days, customer-relevant appearance and taste, application effort and net value recovered.

efforts.label: Implementation priorities
efforts.body: Establish a fruit-specific formulation, application arrangements, supply capacity and relevant food-use documentation. Agree acceptance criteria with the quality team and maintain the intended storage controls. Limit commercial shelf-life claims to tested fruits and conditions. Treat vegetables, meat, seafood and prepared meals as separate technology-selection projects.

title: Understand Profitability by Product and Sales Channel
headline: Understand Profitability by Product and Sales Channel
question: How might we calculate reliable product and channel contribution margins to guide pricing, sourcing and operating decisions?
background: An Indonesian healthy-food retailer sells raw ingredients, grocery products and prepared foods through different channels. This project focuses on product and channel costing, with the finance and operating teams defining the priority decisions and establishing the accuracy of current records.

The objective is to connect revenue with the relevant ingredient, purchasing, yield, handling, processing, packaging, delivery, fee and promotion costs. Clear costing enables the business to compare options on their financial effect alongside sales volume.

Relevant startup capabilities include product-cost modelling, finance-data integration and scenario analysis. Agree how contribution margin is defined, which costs are included and which records support a reliable baseline.

significance.label: Less informed pricing
significance.body: Missing costs give the business an incomplete view of product economics when assessing prices and promotions.

significance.label: Unclear channel trade-offs
significance.body: Inconsistent costing makes it difficult to compare channels with different delivery charges, commissions and discount structures.

significance.label: Overstated improvement claims
significance.body: Inconsistent treatment of yield, allocated costs and shared benefits inflates reported savings.

efforts.label: Available modelling capability
efforts.body: An existing cost-management platform organises cost inputs, assumptions, scenario comparisons and approvals. Configure recipes, saleable output, packaging and channel costs to create a retailer-specific food-product margin model.

efforts.label: First application
efforts.body: Select one prepared-food product and one channel, agree the costing method and reconcile the model with actual purchasing, production and finance records. Compare a limited pricing, ingredient or packaging scenario using transparent assumptions.

efforts.label: Implementation priorities
efforts.body: Establish data ownership, update frequency and the treatment of wastage, returns and shared costs. Assign responsibility for the commercial decision supported by the model and track its realised effect. Use financial scenarios and measured outcomes to guide savings initiatives and decisions on offer expansion.
